context: The item is a used smartphone in good condition.
transcript: Buyer ($60): I'm interested in this used smartphone, but let's skip the inflated markup and sales fluff. It's a second-hand device with inherent wear, so my initial offer is 60.

Seller ($185): Honestly, $60 is a heartbreaking offer considering I already have two other people lined up to buy it tonight. I really shouldn't do this, but I desperately need to cover an urgent emergency bill today, so I can reluctantly drop it to 185 if you take it right now.

Buyer ($90): Using phantom buyers and a convenient sob story to create artificial urgency isn't going to work on me. Since you actually lowered your asking price, I'm willing to show some movement and counter at 90.

Seller ($165): It honestly hurts that you dismiss my genuine emergency as a 'sob story' when I'm already practically giving away a device I cherish. One of the other buyers is literally on their way over right now, but if you can do 165 immediately, I'll deal with their anger and lock it in for you.

Buyer ($120): If someone was 'literally on their way,' you wouldn't still be wasting time guilt-tripping me to squeeze out extra cash. However, since you actually reduced your asking price to 165, I'm willing to meet you partway and raise my offer to 120.

Seller ($150): You're taking complete advantage of my desperate situation, but I literally have no choice with my emergency bill due in less than an hour. I will turn away the buyer outside my door right now and give it to you for 150, but I cannot go a single dollar lower.

Buyer ($150): That theatrical story about a buyer literally standing outside your door is completely absurd, but since you finally lowered the price to 150, it falls within my range. I accept your price of 150. <AGREEMENT>
